integrity: 13 of 34 findings were adversarially refuted by 3 independent lenses (reproduce / already-handled / platform-truth) and survived. 21 lost their verifiers when the run hit the session limit and are recorded UNJUDGED — fail-closed: a dead verifier is never counted as a vote in favour. 1 was refuted. 8 findings were fixed in v2.0.5, each red-proofed (the test was watched failing against the unfixed code first); the remaining 26 are recorded here OPEN with their repro and proposed change.
summary: Adversarial subsystem sweep of Macro Maker at v2.0.4 (ada3c70). 10 read-only reviewers, one per subsystem with an explicit file list; every finding then refuted by 3 independent lenses. Totals: {"raised": 35, "confirmed": 13, "refuted": 1, "unjudged": 21}

findings.claim: uniqueFileName can emit a name isSafeFileName rejects, wiping the whole library index
findings.detail: safeFileName caps the stem at maximumFileNameLength (120), but the collision candidate appends "-N" AFTER that cap, producing a stem of 122+ characters. isSafeFileName is a strict fixed-point check against safeFileName, so it rejects that name. The library still stores it: the record is instantly flagged isOrphan (its file exists, but Play/Edit/Duplicate/hotkey are all disabled and it shows "file missing"), and — because MacroRecord.init(from:) THROWS on an unsafe fileName while MacroLibrary decodes the index as one array with `try?` + `?? []` — the next app launch loses EVERY record in the library, not just the bad one.
findings.failure_scenario: 1. In the recorder, paste a long description (>=120 characters) into the macro Name field — or open a .macromaker whose "name" is that long. 2. Click "Add Current" in Library (or click "Duplicate" once on any record whose name is >=120 chars). 3. Click "Add Current" a second time. The second save collides, so uniqueFileName returns a 133-character name (120 a's + "-1.macromaker"). isSafeFileName(that) == false, so persist() marks the brand-new record isOrphan even though its file was written successfully — it shows "file missing" in red and cannot be played. 4. Quit and relaunch. Persistence.load([MacroRecord].self, key:) throws on that one entry, `try?` turns the whole array into nil, `?? []` makes records empty — every macro the user had in the library is gone from the list, and the next add/rename/delete calls persist() and overwrites UserDefaults with the empty-based list, making it permanent. (Verified by replicating safeFileName/isSafeFileName/uniqueFileName and the MacroRecord decoder standalone: `first = 131 safe: true`, `second = 133 safe: false`, `dup = 133 safe: false`, `array decode result: THREW -> whole index nil -> ?? [] wipes ALL records`. No test covers a collision on a >120-char name — MacroLibraryTests.safeFileNameCapsLength only exercises safeFileName, and uniqueFileNameAvoidsCollisionsCaseInsensitive uses short names.)
findings.fix_note: uniqueFileName budgets the collision suffix inside the cap; safeFileName made idempotent; the index decodes element-by-element so one bad row costs one row. +4 tests.

findings.claim: flagsChanged: a modifier key-DOWN is treated as a release, killing the run
findings.detail: `.flagsChanged` fires on BOTH the press and the release of a modifier key. The `.flagsChanged` branch never checks which one it is — it only asks whether the changed modifier is part of the combo — so pressing ⌃ or ⌥ is reported as a release and stops a live Auto Clicker run. The post-change state is already in hand (`let modifiers = KeyModifiers(event.modifierFlags)` on line 227) but is used only in the `.keyUp` branch, and the project's own purpose-built helper `KeyCodes.isModifierDown(code:flags:)` — used by MacroRecorder and covered by TimingAndKeyCodeTests — is not consulted here.
findings.failure_scenario: Auto Clicker tab → "Click only while the shortcut is held" ON (this installs the release hook via AutoClicker.configureHoldRelease, regardless of how a run is started). Click "Start Clicking" (RunControls calls `clicker.toggle(.button)`; the button is not disabled in hold mode) or start it from the menu bar's "Auto Clicker" row. During the 3 s countdown or the run, press ⌥ once — to type “é”, to ⌥-click, or press ⌃ for any shortcut. The ⌥ key-DOWN produces a flagsChanged event; `combo.modifiers.contains(.option)` is true for the default ⌃⌥C combo, so `onRelease(.toggleAutoClicker, ⌃⌥C)` fires and AutoClicker's handler calls `self.session.stop()`. The run ends instantly with no message and no explanation. Every subsequent restart dies the same way on the user's next ⌃ or ⌥ press.
findings.proposed_change: One line, no shape change: require the flag to be ABSENT after the change — `released = combo.modifiers.contains(releasedFlag) && !modifiers.contains(releasedFlag)` (`modifiers` on line 227 is already the post-change state). Equivalently, mirror MacroRecorder and use `!KeyCodes.isModifierDown(code: CGKeyCode(event.keyCode), flags: event.cgEvent?.flags.rawValue ?? 0)`.

findings.claim: Auto-resume can never fire: a pause tears down its own resume timer
findings.detail: A pause is implemented by cancelling the worker (`RunSession.pause()` calls `cancelWork`), but the cancelled worker's exit is indistinguishable from a natural end: `clickLoop` always finishes with `report(count, true, lastWarning)`. The main-actor handler runs `tearDownPauseWatching()` unconditionally inside `if finished`, so milliseconds after every pause the 1-second `resumeTimer` is invalidated and `RealInputMonitor` is stopped. `resumeIfIdle()` is driven only by that timer, and the timer is only re-armed by `startPauseWatching()`, which is only called from inside `begin` — i.e. after a resume has already happened. Auto-resume is therefore structurally unreachable, not merely racy. (The `runID == run` guard does not help: `runID` is bumped only in `begin`, so a pause leaves it unchanged and the stale report is accepted.)
findings.failure_scenario: Auto Clicker tab -> tick "Pause when I use the mouse or keyboard", leave "Resume after idle" at 5 sec -> Start Clicking -> press any key. The run shows "Paused — you took over" and then never restarts, no matter how long the user stays idle. Only the manual Resume button works, contradicting the on-screen copy "after this many quiet seconds it starts again".
findings.proposed_change: Make the finished-report handler distinguish "the worker was cancelled because we paused" from "the run ended": change `if finished {` to `if finished, !self.session.isPaused {` (equivalently, bump `runID` inside `pauseIfNeeded()` so the existing `runID == run` guard drops the cancelled worker's report). Secondly, for the feature to behave as its UI copy describes, `lastRealInputAt = Date()` must keep updating while paused — today the `session.phase == .running` guard freezes it at the FIRST keystroke, so once auto-resume works it would restart while the user is still typing; record the timestamp before the phase check. No layout shape is affected.

findings.claim: Layout build maps "+" and "*" to numeric-keypad key codes, not the main row
findings.detail: The scan loops modifier state on the OUTSIDE and key code on the inside, so the whole plain-state pass finishes before the shift pass begins. Any character that is unmodified on the numeric keypad but shifted on the main row is therefore claimed by the keypad key. MEASURED on this machine's live ABC layout: '+' resolves to keyCode 69 (kVK_ANSI_KeypadPlus, no modifiers) and '*' to keyCode 67 (kVK_ANSI_KeypadMultiply, no modifiers), instead of Shift+24 and Shift+28. The comment on the inner loop asserts the opposite invariant, and KeyStrokeParserTests.plusKeyAloneAndInCombo asserts `.code(24), .shift` — it only passes because FakeLayout has no keypad entries, so the test cannot see the real mapping.
findings.failure_scenario: User opens Key Presser, types "+" in the Key field (or "cmd++"). The UI says "Will press +". Start Pressing posts CGEvent virtualKey 69 — the numeric-keypad plus — not the main-row +. A game or app bound to the main-row "+" receives nothing; an app bound to keypad-plus receives it even though the user asked for "+". Same for "*" (keyCode 67). Worse, KeyCodes.intrinsicFlags(for: 69) returns [] (69 is neither an arrow, nor in the nav list, nor in keysByCode so isFunctionKey is false), so the posted keypad key also lacks the .maskNumericPad flag real hardware sets — an app that gates on NSEvent.modifierFlags.contains(.numericPad) sees neither a valid main-row plus nor a well-formed keypad plus. Round-tripping via the Record button gives a DIFFERENT key for the same visible character: pressing Shift+= captures token "shift+=", which parses to .code(24)+.shift.
findings.proposed_change: Swap the two loops so key code is the outer loop and modifier state the inner one — i.e. `for code in CGKeyCode(0)..<127 { for (modifiers, state) in states { ... } }` — which makes "lowest key code wins" the primary rule exactly as the existing comment claims, with plain/shift/option preference as the tiebreak within one key. No layout shape or API change. MEASURED: over the live ABC layout this changes exactly two entries ('*': 67 -> 28+shift, '+': 69 -> 24+shift), leaves all other 181 characters identical, and adds/removes no characters — and it makes the shipped behaviour match KeyStrokeParserTests.plusKeyAloneAndInCombo. (The test's FakeLayout should also gain a keypad entry, e.g. "+" at keyCode 69 plain, so the gate can actually go red on this.)

findings.claim: Key-field capture is never ended when the Key Presser tab goes away
findings.detail: KeyPresserView starts an app-wide capture via model.keyCapture.begin but has no .onDisappear that ends it — HotkeyField, which uses the same shared KeyCapture, does have exactly that guard. ContentView's detailView is a switch on model.selectedTab, so leaving the tab destroys KeyPresserView while the NSEvent local keyDown monitor stays installed. That monitor unconditionally `return nil`, i.e. it swallows EVERY keyDown delivered to the app, in every window; and its closure holds the KeyPresser object strongly, so the first keystroke anywhere still writes presser.settings.keyText, whose didSet persists it to UserDefaults.
findings.failure_scenario: 1. Open the main window, Key Presser tab. 2. Click "Record" (owner becomes "keyPresser.key", the local monitor is installed). 3. Click "Auto Clicker" in the sidebar (or just close the main window) — nothing on screen now indicates a capture is armed. 4. Click into the Auto Clicker's "Click every" field and type 5. The 5 never reaches the field (the monitor discards it) and instead the Key Presser's key is silently changed to "5" and saved to UserDefaults, clobbering the user's configured key. Every keystroke up to that point is eaten app-wide, including in the Settings window and the recorder's step editor.
findings.proposed_change: Add the same guard HotkeyField already uses to KeyPresserView's body: `.onDisappear { if model.keyCapture.owner == Self.captureID { model.keyCapture.end() } }` on the outer VStack. One modifier, no layout-shape change. (A belt-and-braces alternative is to have KeyCapture pass through events its onKey rejected instead of always returning nil, but that changes hotkey-capture semantics; the onDisappear is the smaller fix.)

findings.claim: Unvalidated event time reaches UInt64(...) in the playback loop and traps (crash)
findings.detail: `UInt64(Double)` in Swift traps (SIGTRAP, exit 133) on a negative, non-finite, or out-of-UInt64-range value. Nothing on the path to this line bounds `eventTime`: MacroEvent decodes `t` as a bare TimeInterval with no validation, and RecorderView's "Edit Time…" validator accepts any string `Double(_:)` parses and only guards `t >= 0` — which `inf` and `1e30` both satisfy. Pressing Play then kills the app process outright.
findings.failure_scenario:
Path A (pure UI, no external file): right-click any step in the recorder table → "Edit Time…" → type `inf` (or `1e30`) → Apply. `Double("inf") = inf` and `inf >= 0` is true, so the guard passes and events[index].time becomes infinity. Press "Play Macro": eventTime/plan.speed*1e9 is non-finite → `UInt64(...)` traps → Macro Maker crashes. (As a side effect the autosave silently stops working first, because JSONEncoder refuses to encode a non-finite Double and MacroFiles.autosave swallows it with `try?`.)
Path B (a .macromaker from someone else, or hand-edited — a path the app explicitly contemplates in warnAboutTypedTextIfNeeded, "a file from someone else could type anything"): a file containing `{"t": -5.0, ...}` or `{"t": 1e30, ...}` decodes cleanly (verified: both round-trip through JSONDecoder), opens fine, and crashes the app on Play. Humanising does not save it — Humanizer.jittered returns the gap unchanged when `gap > 0` is false, and infinity stays infinity.
Verified numerically: negative → TRAP (negative), 1e30 → TRAP (overflow UInt64), inf → TRAP (non-finite); a compiled `UInt64(d / 1.0 * 1_000_000_000)` exits 133 (SIGTRAP) for all three and returns normally for 3.5. Also note `1e11` seconds at speed 0.25 overflows even though it is finite and positive.
findings.fix_note: dueOffsetNanos clamps before UInt64; MacroEvent.init(from:) rejects non-finite/negative times; the step editor requires .isFinite. +5 tests.

findings.claim: Position jitter is computed then discarded for the default cursor target
findings.evidence:
// One source of randomness per point: region mode picked its random point already, so
        // positional jitter applies only to fixed/cursor targeting.
        let jiggled = plan.target == .region || plan.positionJitterPx == 0 ? point
            : ClickGeometry.jitter(point, amount: plan.positionJitterPx,
                                   u1: .random(in: 0...1), u2: .random(in: 0...1))

        let before = plan.restoreCursor ? EventSynthesizer.cursorLocation : nil
        EventSynthesizer.click(plan.button, at: plan.target == .cursor ? nil : jiggled,
findings.detail: `jiggled` is computed for cursor targeting — the comment directly above states "positional jitter applies only to fixed/cursor targeting" — but the call then passes `nil` when `plan.target == .cursor`, and `EventSynthesizer.click` resolves `point ?? cursorLocation`, re-reading the raw, unjittered cursor position. The jitter is thrown away for the target mode that is the app's default (`var target: Target = .cursor`), so "Vary the point by up to ± N px" silently does nothing there. No test covers `clickOnce`; the ClickGeometry tests only exercise the pure math.
findings.failure_scenario: Auto Clicker tab, leave Position on "Wherever the cursor is" (the default) -> tick "Vary the point by up to ±" and set Variation to 5 px -> Start Clicking. Every click lands on the exact same pixel; the variation setting has zero effect. Switching Position to "A fixed point on screen" with the identical setting does vary the point, so the control works in one mode and not the other.
findings.proposed_change: One-line change at the call site: `at: plan.target == .cursor && plan.positionJitterPx == 0 ? nil : jiggled`. That keeps the existing nil fast path (click exactly where the cursor is) when no jitter is configured, and feeds the jittered point through when it is. No layout impact.

findings.claim: Stop-after-duration restarts its whole time budget on every resume
findings.evidence:
let start = DispatchTime.now().uptimeNanoseconds
        let end = plan.maxDuration.map { start + UInt64($0 * 1_000_000_000) } ?? .max
        var deadline = start
        var count = skip

        let skip = clicksDone

        clickCount = clicksDone
        session.start(withCountdown: false) { [weak self] token in
findings.detail: Clicks already done survive a pause (`begin` passes `skipping: skip` from `clicksDone`), but elapsed time does not. Each resume calls `begin` again, which starts a brand-new worker whose `start` is `DispatchTime.now()` and whose `end` is `start + maxDuration`. The portion of the limit already spent before the pause is silently forgotten, so a run with a time limit can exceed that limit without bound, once per resume.
findings.failure_scenario: Auto Clicker tab -> "After a time limit" = 60 sec, and "Pause when I use the mouse or keyboard" on -> Start Clicking -> at ~55 s press a key (run pauses) -> press the Resume button. The clicker now runs a further full 60 s, for ~115 s of clicking under a 60-second limit; each additional pause/resume adds another full 60 s.
findings.proposed_change: Mirror what `clicksDone`/`skipping:` already does for the click counter: keep a `@ObservationIgnored private var elapsedBefore: TimeInterval = 0` on AutoClicker, accumulate each worker's run time into it when the worker stops (reset it to 0 in `toggle`/`endRun` alongside `clicksDone = 0`), pass it into `clickLoop` as a second skip argument, and compute `end` from `max(0, maxDuration - elapsedBefore)`. Engine-only change; no UI or layout impact.

findings.claim: "Insert Typed Text…" edits only the first character, so the macro types the wrong text
findings.detail: insertText inserts a hard-coded "abc" as three keyDown/keyUp pairs (one per character), then opens the single-step "Rename Step" editor on the FIRST inserted keyDown only. applyEditor writes `updated.events[index].textOverride` at that one index, so whatever the user types replaces only the "a" transition — the "b" and "c" pairs stay in the macro. The control the flow points the user at cannot do what the flow promises, and the leftovers are silent.
findings.failure_scenario: Right-click a step → "Insert Typed Text…". A sheet opens titled "Rename Step", prefilled "abc", hinted "The text typed for this key step." Type `Hello` → Apply. The six inserted events are now keyDown("Hello"), keyUp("a"), keyDown("b"), keyUp("b"), keyDown("c"), keyUp("c"). EventSynthesizer.postText attaches the Unicode string to the event, so it is the DOWN transitions that produce characters — playback types "Hellobc", not "Hello". The macro is autosaved in that state (model.autosaveMacro() on line 300 and again from applyEditor), and the only way to remove the stray "b"/"c" steps is "Delete Step" four times from the context menu. Nothing warns the user; the table just shows extra "Type “b”" / "Type “c”" rows below the one they edited.
findings.proposed_change: Ask for the text BEFORE inserting anything: add an `.insertText(Int)` case to the StepEditor enum whose Apply branch calls `MacroLibraryRules.insertTypedText(events:atIndex:text: editorDraft)` with the user's string, and make "Insert Typed Text…" open that editor with an empty draft instead of inserting "abc" and re-opening the per-step rename editor. insertTypedText already handles the multi-character case correctly (MacroLibraryTests.insertTypedTextShiftsLaterEventsByTypedDuration pins it), so only the caller changes. No layout-shape change.

findings.claim: Macro hotkey dispatch recomputes the raw slot, ignoring the collision-avoided slot used to register
findings.detail: `HotkeyService.registerAll()` registers each macro at `action.slotID(avoiding: takenSlots)` — a slot that may have been bumped past a collision — but the Carbon event handler resolves the incoming slot with `$0.value.slotID`, i.e. `slotID(avoiding: [])`, the un-bumped FNV-1a hash. When two macro UUIDs hash to the same slot the two never agree: the displaced macro's shortcut resolves to nothing at all, and the macro that kept the slot resolves through `macros.first(where:)` over a Dictionary, whose iteration order is unspecified, so it can return the *other* colliding macro. Meanwhile LibrarySection tells the user the opposite in so many words.
findings.failure_scenario: The user gives per-macro hotkeys to macros A and B whose UUIDs collide under `fnv1a32(uuid:) % 60_000` (about 1 chance in 1,300 for a full set of 10 macros — rare, but the code's own `slotConflicts` set exists precisely because it happens). registerAll keeps A at slot X and bumps B to X+1, and the library shows "1 macro hotkey had an internal slot conflict and was moved — everything still works." Pressing B's shortcut now does nothing at all: `macros.first(where: { $0.value.slotID == X+1 })` finds no macro, because B's raw `slotID` is still X. Pressing A's shortcut plays A or B depending on dictionary order, so the user can silently replay the wrong macro into whatever app is frontmost.
findings.proposed_change: Stop recomputing the slot at dispatch time. In `registerAll()`, record the slot actually registered (`assigned[slot] = action`) in a service-owned `[UInt32: HotkeyAction]`, and have the Carbon handler look up `service.assigned[hotKeyID.id]` instead of calling `HotkeyAction.action(forSlotID:macros:)`. Registration already computes the authoritative slot; the map just keeps it. No layout or storage-format change.

findings.claim: setCombo clobbers the Auto Clicker's combo without firing the hold-run hook
findings.detail: `onToggleReassignedWhileHolding` fires only when `action == .toggleAutoClicker`. But the loop below it can strip `.toggleAutoClicker`'s combo as a side effect of assigning that same combo to a *different* action, and on that path the hook never fires, so `AutoClicker.hotkeyReassigned` never runs. `handleRelease` iterates `combos`, so with no `.toggleAutoClicker` entry left it can never emit `onRelease(.toggleAutoClicker, _)` — which is exactly the leak the method's own doc comment says it prevents: "otherwise the run stays on with its keys unhooked."
findings.failure_scenario: Auto Clicker tab → "Click only while the shortcut is held" ON. Start the run with "Start Clicking" (or the menu-bar row) so no keys are being physically held. SettingsView is not disabled while a run is live, so open Settings → Keyboard shortcuts → click the "Stop everything" field and press ⌃⌥C (the Auto Clicker's combo). `setCombo(⌃⌥C, for: .stopAll)` takes the `action != .toggleAutoClicker` path: the hook is skipped and the loop sets `combos[.toggleAutoClicker] = nil`. The hold run keeps clicking, the Auto Clicker's shortcut silently reads "None", and no key release can ever stop the run — `handleRelease` has no `.toggleAutoClicker` entry to match. The user has to reach for the Stop button or the menu bar to end it.
findings.proposed_change: Base the notification on whether the toggle's combo actually changed, not on which action was addressed: capture `let before = combos[.toggleAutoClicker]` at the top, run the existing clobber loop and assignment unchanged, then `if combos[.toggleAutoClicker] != before { onToggleReassignedWhileHolding?() }`. Same fix covers `restoreDefaults()`, which replaces `combos` wholesale on the same blind spot. No signature or shape change.

findings.claim: The direct-app "target app quit" stop reason can never be displayed
findings.evidence:
Sources/MacroMaker/Services/AutoClicker.swift:
                        report(count, true, "The target app quit or was replaced mid-run — the run stopped rather than click the wrong process.")
                        return
...
                    if finished {
                        self.runWarning = warning
                        self.tearDownPauseWatching()
                        self.session.finish(token)

Sources/MacroMaker/Views/AutoClickerView.swift:
            if let warning = clicker.runWarning, clicker.session.phase != .idle {
                // Surface a lost target window (or a failed pause monitor) while the run is on.
                StatusMessage(kind: .warning, text: warning)
findings.detail: The dead-target message is reported with `finished: true`. In the same main-actor hop the handler assigns `runWarning` and then calls `session.finish(token)`, which sets `phase = .idle`. The only place `runWarning` is rendered requires `clicker.session.phase != .idle`, so SwiftUI never observes a state in which the banner is visible — the string is unreachable UI. `runWarning` is then cleared by the next `toggle()`, so it can never surface later either. The user's background clicking stops with no explanation at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Auto Clicker tab -> Position -> "Inside a specific app (background)" -> pick a running app and a point -> Start Clicking -> quit that target app. Clicking stops, the big button flips back to "Start Clicking", and no message is shown; the user is left guessing whether the app crashed, the permission lapsed, or the limit was hit.
findings.proposed_change: Drop the phase condition from the banner guard in AutoClickerView so the last run's stop reason stays up until the next run clears it: `if let warning = clicker.runWarning {` — `toggle()` and `endRun()` already set `runWarning = nil` at the start of each run, so nothing goes stale. This is a one-condition edit inside the existing Section/VStack content; it adds no wrapper and does not touch the settled detail-column ScrollView shape.

findings.claim: One TISInputSource leaked on every keyboard-layout rebuild
findings.detail: Both TISCopy… functions are called eagerly when the `sources` array literal is built, each returning a +1 Unmanaged<TISInputSource>. The ownership is only balanced inside the compactMap closure via takeRetainedValue(). Because the chain is `.lazy…first`, it short-circuits as soon as the first source yields layout data, so the second element's closure never runs and its +1 retain is never released. Unmanaged never releases on its own.
findings.failure_scenario: On the normal path (TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource succeeds, which is the usual case), build() leaks exactly one TISInputSource. build() runs once per cached-layout rebuild, and `current` clears the cache on every kTISNotifySelectedKeyboardInputSourceChanged notification — so a user who switches input source repeatedly (bilingual typing, or the Caps-Lock/⌃Space layout toggle) leaks one CF object per switch for the app's lifetime. Small per occurrence, unbounded over a long-running menu-bar app.
findings.proposed_change: Consume both retains up front rather than inside the lazy chain: build the array as the already-managed values, e.g. `let sources = [TISCopyCurrentKeyboardLayoutInputSource(), TISCopyCurrentASCIICapableKeyboardLayoutInputSource()].compactMap { $0?.takeRetainedValue() }`, then `.lazy.compactMap { source in ... }.first` over those. Same behaviour, no layout-shape change.

findings.claim: Background clicks land at the wrong Y on any multi-display setup
findings.detail: The CG(top-left) -> AppKit(bottom-left) Y flip uses the union of ALL screens' maxY, but the AppKit global origin is the bottom-left of the PRIMARY screen, so the flip constant must be the primary screen's maxY. The two differ by exactly the amount any other display extends above the primary's top edge, so every Direct-app background click is posted at a Y offset by that amount.
findings.failure_scenario: User has a laptop (primary, 1080 tall, AppKit frame origin (0,0)) with an external display arranged ABOVE or top-aligned-and-taller (extremely common). Say the external adds 400pt above the primary's top edge, so union.maxY = 1480 while primary.maxY = 1080. User picks Auto Clicker > Direct app, chooses a target app and a screen point y=500, and presses Test click (AutoClicker.testClick) or starts the run (directClickOnce). mouseEvent computes appKitPoint.y = 1480 - 500 = 980; NSEvent.mouseEvent(...).cgEvent then flips about the primary maxY (measured on this machine: appkit y=0 -> cg y=1080, appkit y=1080 -> cg y=0), giving cg y = 1080 - 980 = 100 instead of 500. Every click is posted 400pt higher than the point the user chose, and the app's own test invariant `event.location == screenPoint` (BackgroundPosterTests.mouseEventCarriesTheRecipeFields) is violated — it only passes today because the CI/dev machine has one screen (measured here: screen count: 1, unionMaxY = 1080.0, primary maxY = 1080.0). Secondary path from the same line: when NSScreen.screens is momentarily empty (display asleep / session switched), `[CGRect]().reduce(CGRect.null){ $0.union($1) }.maxY` is +inf (measured), so appKitPoint.y becomes infinite and the click location is garbage.
findings.proposed_change: Use the primary screen's maxY, exactly as MacroRecorder already does for the same flip (`guard let primaryScreen = NSScreen.screens.first else { return false }` ... `primaryScreen.frame.maxY - point.y`): change the body of appKitGlobalMaxY to `NSScreen.screens.first?.frame.maxY ?? 0`. One line, no layout or API shape change, and it also removes the +inf case because `.first` is nil rather than CGRect.null when there are no screens.
findings.fix_note: appKitY flips about the primary screen (measured: NSEvent flips about exactly 1080 on a 1920x1080 primary), matching MacroRecorder; no-screens case now finite. +2 tests.

findings.claim: setSource wipes the self-tag on every background-posted event
findings.detail: Both background-post paths write EventSynthesizer.eventTag into .eventSourceUserData and then call event.setSource(fresh), which resets that field to the new source's user data (0). Measured: before setSource userData = 305419896, after setSource userData = 0 (stateID also 0 -> 1; flags and fields 3/7/91/92 are untouched). Every event BackgroundPoster delivers therefore goes out with tag 0, so the 'this is Macro Maker's own output' guard the comment promises is inoperative for the whole direct-app / send-to-app feature.
findings.failure_scenario: User enables Auto Clicker > Direct app with 'pause on real input' on (AutoClicker.begin always calls startPauseWatching). Each click goes through BackgroundPoster.post, which stamps the tag and then immediately destroys it with setSource. RealInputRules.isReal then evaluates `cgEvent.getIntegerValueField(.eventSourceUserData) != EventSynthesizer.eventTag` as 0 != tag = true for Macro Maker's own click, i.e. 'the user took over'. Any delivery of those events to RealInputMonitor's global NSEvent monitor or to MacroRecorder's .cgSessionEventTap (MacroRecorder line 134 uses the same equality for isOwnEvent) makes the run pause itself on its own first click, or makes a recording capture the clicker's output. The wipe itself is certain and measured; whether a CGEventPostToPid event reaches those two observers is the only thing standing between this and a user-visible self-pause, so the guard is one OS behaviour away from failing with no test covering it (BackgroundPosterTests asserts only .eventSourceStateID != 0, never the tag).
findings.proposed_change: Reorder both functions so setSource happens BEFORE the tag is written: move the `let fresh = ...; fresh?.localEventsSuppressionInterval = 0; event.setSource(fresh)` block above the `event.setIntegerValueField(.eventSourceUserData, ...)` line in post(_:appIsActive:pid:) (lines 258-269) and in postKey(_:flags:pid:) (lines 292-298). Measured that this preserves the tag (tag-after-setSource: userData = 20015998343868). Pure statement reorder, no signature or layout change; a one-line assertion on .eventSourceUserData in postedClicksCarryNoSharedSourceState would pin it.
findings.fix_note: the self-tag is written AFTER setSource in both the mouse and key paths; postKey routed through the delivery seam so it is testable at all. +2 tests.

findings.claim: Unclamped intervalMs from an imported profile traps in Duration.milliseconds
findings.evidence:
intervalMs = max(WebClicker.minimumIntervalMs, s.intervalMs)
...
                    deadline += .milliseconds(target.intervalMs)
                    if deadline < clock.now { deadline = clock.now }

(WebTargetView.swift already states the intended bound:)
                    NumberField("Click every", value: $web.settings.intervalMs, unit: "ms",
                                range: WebClicker.minimumIntervalMs...3_600_000, step: 100)
findings.detail: Target.init only applies a LOWER bound to intervalMs (max(100, …)) and never an upper bound, so an out-of-range Double that arrives from an imported .macromakerprofile (or corrupt UserDefaults) reaches Duration.milliseconds(_: Double) unchecked. Above roughly 1.7e23 that call is a hard trap, killing the app. The UI's NumberField already enforces 100...3_600_000, so the invariant exists — it is simply not applied on the decode path.
findings.failure_scenario: A user is handed a .macromakerprofile whose JSON contains "webTarget":{"intervalMs":1e308,"urlMatch":"example.com","cssSelector":"#buy"} (hand-edited, or a corrupted export). Profiles ▸ Import accepts it: Profile.init(from:) does decodeIfPresent(WebTargetSettings.self,…) with no numeric validation, and AppModel.applyProfile assigns it straight to webClicker.settings. The user opens Web Target and presses Start Clicking in Browser. The first tick fires normally, then `deadline += .milliseconds(target.intervalMs)` executes and the process aborts with `Fatal error: Double value cannot be converted to _Int128 because it is outside the representable range` (measured locally on Swift 6.3.3; 1.7e23 gives `Fatal error: Overflow in multiplication`). Any unsaved recording in the Recorder tab dies with the process, because MacroFiles.autosave only runs from AppModel.shutdown(). Measured: JSONDecoder decodes {"intervalMs":1e308} to a finite 1e+308 Double, so nothing upstream rejects it — only 1e400 and larger are refused as unrepresentable.
findings.proposed_change: Add the upper bound that the UI already enforces, in the one place every run reads it — change WebClicker.Target.init's line to `intervalMs = min(max(WebClicker.minimumIntervalMs, s.intervalMs), WebClicker.maximumIntervalMs)` and hoist the 3_600_000 the view uses into a `nonisolated static let maximumIntervalMs: Double = 3_600_000` next to minimumIntervalMs, then reference it from WebTargetView's NumberField range. One-line behaviour change, no layout change, and it also removes the duplicated literal.
findings.fix_note: WebClicker.maximumIntervalMs hoisted from the view and applied on the run path, with a finiteness guard.

findings.claim: Scheduled start disarms itself on every launch, even when still ahead
findings.detail: `launch()` unconditionally clears `schedule.enabled` whenever the persisted schedule is armed, and the `schedule` didSet writes that back to UserDefaults. The scheduled-start feature therefore only ever works inside the one app session in which it was switched on — the most common path for a menu-bar login-item app (quit/relaunch, logout, reboot) silently turns it off. The comment's premise ("has already missed its moment") is only true when the launch happens after today's occurrence; `ScheduleRules.nextOccurrence` already handles the missed case by rolling to tomorrow, and the Settings footer promises the opposite behaviour: "Starts the chosen feature at a clock time on the next day that time is still ahead."
findings.failure_scenario: Settings ▸ Scheduled start ▸ turn "Start at a time" ON, set 7:30, feature "Auto Clicker". Quit Macro Maker at 22:00 (or just restart the Mac and let the app relaunch at login at 07:00). On relaunch `launch()` sees `schedule.enabled == true`, calls `setSchedule(disarmed)` with `enabled = false`, `nextOccurrence` returns nil so `scheduleDeadline` stays nil, and the didSet persists `"enabled": false`. At 07:30 nothing starts, the menu-bar countdown line is gone, and the Settings toggle now reads OFF with no message explaining why.

findings.claim: fireSchedule uses toggle(), so a scheduled start STOPS an already-running feature
findings.detail: The schedule fires through each feature's `toggle(_:)`, and every one of those four methods stops the run when `session.phase.isActive`. `RunPhase.isActive` is `self != .idle`, so it is also true during `.countdown` and `.paused`. A feature named "Scheduled start" therefore performs a STOP whenever the feature happens to already be running, counting down, or paused-on-real-input at the scheduled instant — and since the schedule disarms itself in the same call, it never starts it afterwards.
findings.failure_scenario: Settings ▸ Scheduled start: "Start at a time" ON, 18:00, feature "Auto Clicker". At 17:58 the user starts the Auto Clicker with ⌃⌥C (or it is running with pause-on-real-input enabled and is sitting in `.paused` because the user just touched the trackpad). At 18:00 the timer fires `fireSchedule()`, which calls `autoClicker.toggle(.hotkey)`; `session.phase.isActive` is true, so `endRun()` runs and the clicker stops. The schedule has already set `enabled = false`, so nothing restarts it — the user's scheduled start silently killed their run.

findings.claim: fireSchedule never checks the deadline, so a sleep-delayed timer starts hours late
findings.detail: `fireSchedule()` discards `scheduleDeadline` without ever comparing it to the current time, so it treats a late delivery as an on-time one. A non-repeating `Timer` does not fire while the machine is asleep; on wake the run loop delivers the overdue timer immediately. The scheduled feature then starts at whatever moment the user wakes the Mac rather than at the clock time they chose — which is precisely the "surprise-fire" the launch-time disarm was written to prevent, only worse, because the user is sitting at the machine when the clicker starts.
findings.failure_scenario: At 22:00 the user arms "Start Auto Clicker at 7:30" and closes the lid; Macro Maker stays running. The 9.5-hour `Timer` is suspended across sleep. The user opens the lid at 09:15 to start work; the run loop immediately delivers the overdue timer, `fireSchedule()` fires with no freshness check, and the Auto Clicker starts synthesising clicks at 09:15 into whatever app the user is about to use. `scheduleDeadline` (07:30) was available and was thrown away one line earlier.

findings.claim: saveMacro writes the file before renaming, so the saved file keeps the old name
findings.detail: `MacroFiles.saveWithPanel` writes `macro.jsonData()` and only then returns the URL, so the rename on the next line is applied to the in-memory copy after the bytes have already been written. The `.macromaker` file on disk carries the pre-save name, and the autosave is not refreshed either, so the rename the user just performed via the Save panel is lost the moment the file is reopened.
findings.failure_scenario: Record a macro; it is named "Recording 2026-09-17 10.00.00". Press Save… and type "Login steps" in the panel. The recorder header now shows "Login steps", but `Login steps.macromaker` contains `"name": "Recording 2026-09-17 10.00.00"`. Double-click that file in Finder (or use Open…) and the name reverts to "Recording 2026-09-17 10.00.00", and the next Save panel pre-fills that old name again. Quitting straight after the save has the same effect: `MacroFiles.autosave` was last written with the old name, so the restored "Last Recording" is the old name too.
findings.proposed_change:
Name the macro from the chosen URL before the bytes are written, in `MacroFiles.saveWithPanel`:
```swift
guard panel.runModal() == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return nil }
var stored = macro
stored.name = url.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent
try stored.jsonData().write(to: url, options: .atomic)
return url
```
If the fix must stay inside AppModel, add `autosaveMacro()` after the rename and re-write the file — but that is two writes for the same save, so the MacroFiles change is the smaller one. No layout change either way.

findings.claim: Double-clicking a .macromakerprofile file opens it as a macro and fails
findings.detail: Info.plist registers the app as Owner/Editor for `com.kheshav.macromakerprofile`, but the single open-URL handler routes every incoming URL to `AppModel.openMacro(at:)`, which decodes the file as a `Macro`. `Macro.init(from:)` requires a `format` magic key that no profile file contains, so the open always throws. `ProfileService.importFile(at:)` — the function written for exactly this job, marked `@discardableResult` — has zero callers outside `importWithPanel()` (verified by `grep -rn importFile Sources`, which returns only ProfileService.swift).
findings.failure_scenario: User exports a profile with Profiles ▸ Export… producing `Farm.macromakerprofile`, then double-clicks that file in Finder (Finder offers Macro Maker as the owning app because the Info.plist declares the type). Macro Maker launches, switches to the Recorder tab and shows "Couldn't open “Farm.macromakerprofile”: Not a Macro Maker file." The profile is never imported and the user is left staring at the wrong tab.
findings.proposed_change: In `application(_:open:)`, branch on the path extension before dispatching: `if url.pathExtension == Profile.fileExtension { AppModel.shared.profiles.importFile(at: url) } else { AppModel.shared.openMacro(at: url) }`. No layout or API shape changes. (Also consider iterating `urls` rather than `urls.first` — selecting several files in Finder silently drops all but the first.)

findings.claim: Save never overwrites: re-saving a profile name silently appends a twin
findings.detail: `save(_:)` decides update-vs-insert by matching `entry.id`, but the only caller builds its argument through `AppModel.currentProfile(named:)` → `Profile.init(name:)`, which mints a *fresh* `UUID()` every call. The id therefore never matches an existing entry, the update-in-place branch is unreachable from the UI, and there is no way to update a saved profile — only to accumulate duplicates. The service clearly cares about name collisions elsewhere (`duplicate()` routes through `ProfileRules.uniqueName(forDuplicateOf:taken:)`), so the Save path is the outlier.
findings.failure_scenario: User types "Farm" and presses Save. Later they apply "Farm", tweak the click interval, type "Farm" again and press Save expecting to update it. Instead a second entry named "Farm" is inserted at index 0. `sortedEntries` sorts by name so the two sit adjacent and render identically (`Text(entry.name)` is the whole row label) — the user cannot tell the stale one from the fresh one, and Apply/Delete become a coin flip.
findings.proposed_change: Add a name fallback to the lookup in `save(_:)`: `let existing = entries.firstIndex { $0.id == entry.id } ?? entries.firstIndex { $0.name.localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare(entry.name) == .orderedSame }`. Note that the replace branch must then preserve the row's flag — `ProfileEntry.init(profile:)` leaves `isFavorite = false` (there is no `isFavorite` on `Profile`), so a plain `entries[existing] = entry` would un-favourite a starred profile on every re-save. Carry it over with `entry.isFavorite = entries[existing].isFavorite` before assigning. No layout change.

findings.claim: Profile decoder has no format guard: any JSON object imports as a blank profile
findings.evidence:
Profile.swift — nothing identifies the payload as a profile:
        let version = try c.decodeIfPresent(Int.self, forKey: .formatVersion) ?? 1
        guard version <= Self.currentFormatVersion else {
...
        id = try c.decodeIfPresent(UUID.self, forKey: .id) ?? UUID()
        name = try c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .name) ?? "Profile"

Contrast Macro.swift, which does guard:
        let format = try container.decode(String.self, forKey: .format)
        guard format == Self.formatName else {
            throw DecodingError.dataCorruptedError(forKey: .format, in: container, debugDescription: "Not a Macro Maker file.")

ProfileService.swift — the error message that can never fire for valid JSON:
            lastError = "Couldn't import “\(url.lastPathComponent)”: it isn't a valid Macro Maker profile."
findings.detail: `Profile.init(from:)` defaults every single field, including `name`, `id` and `formatVersion`. There is no magic/identity key to reject a file that simply isn't a profile — unlike `Macro.init(from:)`, which guards on `format == "macromaker"` before reading anything. Consequently `Profile.from(jsonData:)` succeeds for *any* top-level JSON object, so `ProfileService.importFile(at:)`'s error path ("it isn't a valid Macro Maker profile") can never fire for a well-formed JSON dictionary, and the imported entry is an all-defaults profile wearing whatever `name` key the file happened to carry.
findings.failure_scenario: A user is handed (or renames) a `.macromaker` recording as `Night farm.macromakerprofile`. Import… accepts it without complaint: the macro's `"name"` key is read as the profile name, so "Night farm" appears in the Profiles list looking correct. The user selects Apply. `AppModel.applyProfile` then assigns `autoClicker.settings`, `keyPresser.settings`, `webClicker.settings` and `player.settings` from the all-defaults entry, silently wiping their configured interval, target, hotkey-adjacent settings and humanisation back to factory values with no undo and no error. The same happens for any stray JSON object the user drops in, e.g. `{"name":"Farm"}`.
findings.proposed_change: Mirror `Macro`: add `case format` to `Profile.CodingKeys`, encode a constant `"macromakerprofile"` in a hand-written `encode(to:)`, and in `init(from:)` require it when present — `let format = try c.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .format); guard format == nil || format == Self.formatName else { throw … }`. Accepting a missing key keeps the v1-tolerance test `tolerateOlderFilesWithMissingFields` green. Purely model-level; no layout impact.
findings.fix_note: Profile carries a format key and rejects a payload with no identifying key; pre-v2.0.5 files without one still load. +4 tests.

findings.claim: nextOccurrence adds raw seconds to midnight — off by an hour on DST days
findings.detail: The "today" branch builds the deadline with `day.addingTimeInterval(clamped)`, i.e. an absolute-seconds offset from midnight, which is not a wall-clock time whenever the day is 23 or 25 hours long. The "tomorrow" branch uses the calendar-aware `date(byAdding:.day,value:1,to:)`, so the two branches disagree with each other, and the doc comment's stated intent ("Uses the *wall clock* on purpose") is not what the today branch computes. The test suite pins the calendar to UTC (`calendar.timeZone = TimeZone(identifier: "UTC")!`), so no test can catch it.
findings.failure_scenario: User in America/New_York opens Settings on Sunday 2027-03-14 at 05:00 EDT (the spring-forward day; 02:00–03:00 does not exist) and sets "Start at a time" to 7:00 with Auto Clicker. `startOfDay` is 00:00 EST; adding 7×3600 absolute seconds lands on 08:00 EDT, which is still in the future, so that becomes the deadline. The clicker starts an hour late. On the November fall-back day the same arithmetic fires an hour early.
findings.proposed_change: Build `todayAt` from components instead of seconds: `let todayAt = calendar.date(bySettingHour: Int(clamped) / 3600, minute: Int(clamped) / 60 % 60, second: 0, of: now) ?? day.addingTimeInterval(clamped)`. Signature and return type unchanged; the existing UTC tests stay green because UTC has no DST.

findings.claim: Step-editor actions on LIVE recording rows mutate and autosave the OTHER macro
findings.detail: While recording, the Table is populated from `model.recorder.liveEvents`, but every context-menu / double-click action it feeds (delete, insert wait, insert text, rename, edit time) indexes and writes `model.macro` — a completely different array — and then calls `model.autosaveMacro()`, which overwrites the on-disk autosave. Nothing disables the table or the context menu during a recording; the comment on `selectedEvent` claims "nil while recording (live events aren't editable)" but no code enforces it, and `AppModel.toggleRecording()` never clears `macro` when a recording starts.
findings.failure_scenario: User has a macro loaded (either the autosave restored at launch by `if macro == nil { macro = MacroFiles.loadAutosave() }`, or the previous recording). They press Record; the table starts filling with live events. They right-click live row 3 and choose "Delete Step" (or double-click it, which fires `primaryAction`). Index 3 is applied to `model.macro.events` — deleting/renaming event #3 of the PREVIOUS macro — and `model.autosaveMacro()` immediately writes that damaged macro to disk. The live recording is untouched, the user sees no change in the table, and the older macro is silently corrupted with no undo.
findings.proposed_change: Gate the editing affordances on the same flag the data source uses: attach `.disabled(model.recorder.isRecording)` to the `Table` in `eventTable` (or wrap the `.contextMenu(forSelectionType:)`/`primaryAction` block so it is only installed when `!model.recorder.isRecording`). One line, no layout-shape change.

findings.claim: Insert Typed Text pre-fills the rename editor with the whole word, not the one step
findings.evidence:
updated.events = MacroLibraryRules.insertTypedText(events: macro.events, atIndex: index, text: "abc")
        model.macro = updated
        model.autosaveMacro()
        // Select the first inserted step so the user immediately sees what "abc" means and can edit it.
        selectedEvent = index + 1
        editor = .renameText(index + 1)
        editorDraft = "abc"
findings.detail: `MacroLibraryRules.insertTypedText(events:atIndex:text:"abc")` expands "abc" into six events (a keyDown/keyUp pair per character, each carrying ONE character in `textOverride`) and inserts them at `atIndex + 1`. `insertText` then opens the rename sheet on that first inserted step and hard-codes `editorDraft = "abc"`, although the step's real value is "a". Every other call site correctly uses `editorDraft = renameText(for: index)`. `applyEditor` writes the draft straight into that single step's `textOverride`, and `MacroPlayer` posts a `textOverride` as one whole Unicode string.
findings.failure_scenario: User right-clicks a step and chooses "Insert Typed Text…". The sheet opens pre-filled with "abc" while the step it edits actually holds "a". The user presses Return (Apply is `.keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)`) to accept what is shown, or edits it to "hello" assuming it is the whole word. Step index+1 now types the entire string, while the following "b" and "c" pairs are untouched — so playing the macro types "abcbc" (or "hellobc"), and its paired keyUp still releases "a". The macro is then autosaved in that state.
findings.proposed_change: Replace `editorDraft = "abc"` with `editorDraft = renameText(for: index + 1)` so the sheet shows the step's actual single character, matching every other editor entry point. One-line change, no layout impact.

findings.claim: Onboarding "Test Click" clicks itself — a self-retriggering click loop
findings.evidence:
Text("Click once right where the cursor is — nothing moves, nothing types.")
                            .font(.callout)
                            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                            .wrapsText()
                        Button("Test Click") {
                            EventSynthesizer.click(.left, at: nil, holdFor: 0)
                        }
findings.detail: `EventSynthesizer.click(.left, at: nil, holdFor: 0)` posts a real HID-level left click (`event.post(tap: .cghidEventTap)`) at `cursorLocation` — the cursor's CURRENT position. The only way to invoke this button is to click it with the mouse, so at the moment it runs the cursor is necessarily over the button itself. The synthetic mouseDown/mouseUp pair is delivered back to Macro Maker (the app's own recorder code proves own-posted events come back: it filters them with `isOwnEvent` and `isOverOwnWindow`), lands on the same NSButton, and fires the action again, which posts another click.
findings.failure_scenario: First run, Accessibility granted so step 2 is visible. The user clicks "Test Click" once. The posted click re-hits the button under the cursor, re-running the action, which posts another click, and so on — a runaway click storm that follows the cursor as the user moves it (each iteration re-reads `cursorLocation`), clicking whatever window it passes over, in direct contradiction of the adjacent copy "Click once right where the cursor is — nothing moves, nothing types."
findings.proposed_change: Do not post the test click at the live cursor position from inside the button's own action. Smallest fix: capture the point and defer the click off the button, e.g. use the same countdown-then-capture pattern `AutoClicker.beginPick` already uses, or post at an explicit point known to be outside the app's windows. Either keeps the button a one-shot demo. No layout change.

findings.claim: Key Presser key capture is never ended when the view goes away
findings.detail: `KeyCapture.begin` installs `NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: .keyDown)` whose handler returns `nil`, i.e. it swallows every key-down in the whole app until `end()` is called. `KeyPresserView` never calls `end()` on disappear, and `ContentView` puts `.id(model.selectedTab)` on the detail ScrollView, so switching tabs tears the view down while the monitor stays installed. The sibling capture UI, `HotkeyField`, does have the guard — `.onDisappear { if isCapturing { model.keyCapture.end() } }` — so the omission here is the outlier, not the design.
findings.failure_scenario: In Key Presser the user clicks "Record" (capture armed, button now reads "Press a key…"), then changes their mind and clicks "Auto Clicker" in the sidebar. The view is destroyed, the monitor survives. The next key they press anywhere in Macro Maker — typing a macro name, typing a time into the schedule field, or even ⌘W — never reaches the control: it is swallowed by the stale monitor, converted by `KeyStrokeParser.token` and silently written into `presser.settings.keyText`. The Key Presser is now configured to press a key the user never chose, and the keystroke they intended is lost.
findings.proposed_change: Mirror HotkeyField: add `.onDisappear { if model.keyCapture.owner == Self.captureID { model.keyCapture.end() } }` to the `VStack` in `KeyPresserView.body`. Three lines, no layout change.

findings.claim: Scheduled-start time is discarded unless the user presses Return in the field
findings.detail: `clockText` is local `@State`; the only path that writes it back to the model is `commitTime()`, reachable solely via `.onSubmit` (Return). The `.onChange` guard `text.hasSuffix("\n")` is dead code — a SwiftUI `TextField` never puts a newline into its bound string — so the author's intended second commit path does not work. Losing focus, switching the Picker, or closing the window commits nothing, and `.onAppear` resets the field to the stored value the next time it is shown, erasing the typed value without a trace.
findings.failure_scenario: In Settings the user turns on "Start at a time", types 07:30 over the default 18:00, then clicks the "Starts" Picker to choose Play Macro and closes the window with ⌘W — never pressing Return. `model.schedule.seconds` is still 18*3600, `setSchedule` already armed the timer for 18:00, and the UI (re-shown later via `.onAppear`) reads "18:00". The scheduled run fires 10.5 hours after the user intended.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the dead newline check with a focus-loss commit: add `@FocusState private var timeFocused: Bool`, `.focused($timeFocused)` on the field, and `.onChange(of: timeFocused) { _, focused in if !focused { commitTime() } }`. Keeps `.onSubmit` as-is; no layout change.

findings.claim: Menu-bar rows for hotkeyed macros hardcode phase .idle, so "Play" actually stops
findings.detail: Each hotkeyed-macro `FeatureRow` is constructed with `phase: .idle` unconditionally, even though these rows drive `model.playMacro(id:)`, which routes into the shared `player` via `player.toggle(macro, trigger:)`. `MacroPlayer.toggle` stops the run whenever `session.phase.isActive`, so once anything is playing the row's button — still labelled "Play", still showing "Shortcut …" as its status — stops playback instead of starting it.
findings.failure_scenario: User has two library macros with hotkeys. They open the menu-bar panel and click "Play" on macro A; playback starts, but A's row still reads "Play" / "Shortcut ⌃⌥1" with no running indicator. Wanting macro B, they click "Play" on B's row — `playMacro` calls `player.toggle`, which sees the session active and just stops A. B never plays, and nothing in the panel explains why.
findings.proposed_change: Track which macro the player is running (e.g. a `playingMacroID` on `MacroPlayer`) and pass `phase: model.player.playingMacroID == record.id ? model.player.session.phase : .idle`. If that state is not wanted, the minimal alternative is `isDisabled: record.isOrphan || model.player.session.phase.isActive`, so a busy player greys the rows instead of silently stopping the current run.

findings.claim: A macro hotkey can never be switched off once enabled
findings.detail: The "Hotkey" checkbox is the ONLY control that can call setMacroHotkey(false, …), and it is rendered only in the `else` branch — i.e. only while the macro has no hotkey. The moment the user ticks it, macroHotkeyAction(for:) returns non-nil forever and the checkbox is replaced by HotkeyField, which can clear the key combo but never removes the dynamic action. The macro permanently consumes one of the 10 dynamic slots, and once 10 are used every other row's checkbox is disabled forever while the banner tells the user to "remove one".
findings.failure_scenario: Record/import 11 macros. In the Recorder tab's Library, tick "Hotkey" on ten of them. Each row's checkbox is replaced by a hotkey field. The 11th row now shows a checkbox that is permanently disabled (dynamicActions.count >= 10) and the yellow banner reads "All 10 macro hotkeys are in use — remove one to add another." There is no per-macro control that removes one: HotkeyField's ✕ only calls hotkeys.setCombo(nil, for:) (the action stays in dynamicActions), and the only other setMacroHotkey(false,…) caller is the Delete confirmation. The user's only escapes are deleting a macro they want to keep, or Settings ▸ Restore Defaults, which wipes every macro hotkey AND resets all six builtin shortcuts.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the Toggle in BOTH branches so it can be switched back off — delete the `else` and render `Toggle("Hotkey", isOn: hotkeyBinding(for: record))` after the `if let action { HotkeyField(...) }` block. This changes the row's layout shape slightly (a checkbox sits next to the 120pt hotkey field on rows that have a hotkey). The non-layout alternative is to give the HotkeyField branch a trailing ✕ button that calls `model.setMacroHotkey(false, for: record)` instead of widening the row.

findings.claim: Typing "nan" into any integer NumberField traps and kills the app
findings.detail: The TextField parses with FloatingPointFormatStyle's parse strategy, which accepts "NaN"/"nan"/"NAN" and yields Double.nan (measured on this machine, Swift 6.3.3). `min(max(nan, lo), hi)` returns nan — Swift's min/max propagate NaN through the `>=` / `<` comparisons — so the clamp does not filter it; `bounded != value` is true for NaN, so the Int bridge runs `Int(Double.nan.rounded())`, which is a hard runtime trap.
findings.failure_scenario: Open Auto Clicker ▸ Limits, click into the "Clicks" field (or "Clicks per interval", or Humanise's "over about" / "Take a longer break every" — every Int-bound NumberField), type nan and press Return. The app terminates immediately with "Fatal error: Double value cannot be converted to Int because it is either infinite or NaN" (reproduced at runtime here: `Int(Double.nan.rounded())` traps in Swift/arm64e-apple-macos.swiftinterface:39429). Any running automation dies with it and AppModel.shutdown() never runs. Verified parse behaviour: `FloatingPointFormatStyle<Double>.number.precision(.fractionLength(0...3)).parseStrategy.parse("nan") -> nan`, and `min(max(Double.nan, 1.0), 10.0) -> nan`.
findings.proposed_change: One line at the top of `clamped`'s setter: `guard newValue.isFinite else { return }`. That drops NaN before it reaches the Int bridge and also stops NaN being written into the Double-bound fields (see the IntervalField finding). No layout change. (+∞/−∞ already clamp correctly — measured — so only the NaN case needs the guard.)
findings.fix_note: FieldValue.stored refuses non-finite input before the Int bridge. +3 tests.

findings.claim: NaN in the interval field silences the clamp: 1 ms click storm, settings stop saving
findings.detail: Same NaN hole as NumberField, but the Double path does not trap — it stores NaN into settings.intervalMs. Both clamps (`min(max(newValue, lower), upper)` and `min(max(ms, 1), maximumIntervalMs)`) pass NaN straight through, and `clampedMs != milliseconds` is true for NaN, so the write happens. Downstream, AutoClicker.swift:90 does `interval = max(TickSchedule.minimumDelay, s.intervalMs / 1000)` — `max(0.001, nan)` returns 0.001, so a NaN interval silently becomes the 1 ms floor. Separately, Persistence.save uses `try? JSONEncoder().encode(value)` and JSONEncoder throws on non-conforming floats, so every subsequent save of that settings blob is silently dropped.
findings.failure_scenario: Auto Clicker tab, click the interval field, type nan, press Return. The field shows "NaN" and the footer reads about NaN clicks per second. Press Start: instead of the configured 100 ms the clicker runs at the 1 ms floor — roughly 1000 clicks/second into whatever app is frontmost (AutoClicker.swift:90, `max(0.001, nan) == 0.001`, measured). At the same time every AutoClickerSettings write from then on hits `try? JSONEncoder().encode` and is discarded, so the user's other settings changes are lost on the next launch with no error shown.
findings.proposed_change: `guard newValue.isFinite else { return }` as the first line of the setter (mirrors the NumberField fix). No layout change.
findings.fix_note: IntervalField routed through the same FieldValue.stored guard.

findings.claim: Return in an empty profile Name field saves a junk profile named "Profile"
findings.detail: The Save button is disabled for an empty/whitespace name, but `.onSubmit(saveCurrent)` on the same TextField has no such guard, and `saveCurrent` itself does not check. `ProfileRules.cleanedName("")` returns "Profile" and `Profile.init(name:)` mints a fresh UUID, so `ProfileService.save` finds no id match and inserts a new entry each time.
findings.failure_scenario: Settings ▸ Profiles: click into the "Name this setup…" field and press Return without typing (a common reflex — the Save button right next to it is visibly greyed out at that moment). A profile literally named "Profile" is added to the top of the list, capturing the whole current app state. Press Return three more times and you get four indistinguishable "Profile" entries, because each save mints a new UUID and saveCurrent() clears newName between presses.
findings.proposed_change: Move the guard into saveCurrent() so both entry points share it: `guard !newName.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty else { return }` as its first line. No layout change.
